claims.statement: Hexarelin is a synthetic hexapeptide GHRP-class growth hormone secretagogue that stimulates growth hormone release both in vitro and in vivo by acting as a ghrelin/growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHS-R1a) agonist.

extractedEvidence.quote: Hexarelin is a new hexapeptide (His-D-2-methyl-Trp-Ala-Trp-D-Phe-Lys-NH2) that stimulates the release of growth hormone both in vitro and in vivo.

Hexarelin is a synthetic hexapeptide that is primarily of interest in the field of endocrinology research. It functions as a ghrelin receptor agonist, which makes it a useful tool for studying the regulation of growth hormone release and appetite control mechanisms.

claims.statement: In a double-blind, placebo-controlled, rising-dose study of 12 healthy adult male volunteers, single intravenous boluses of hexarelin (0.5, 1, and 2 micrograms/kg) produced dose-dependent increases in plasma growth hormone, peaking at about 30 minutes; mean peak GH concentrations were 3.9 (placebo), 26.9, 52.3, and 55.0 ng/mL at increasing doses, with response near-maximal by the 2 microgram/kg dose. This is an acute GH-release pharmacodynamic finding in healthy men, not evidence of any downstream clinical benefit.

context.doseText: single IV bolus of 0.5, 1, or 2 micrograms/kg in a rising-dose study design (trial protocol; not a use recommendation)

extractedEvidence.quote: Twelve adult male volunteers received single intravenous boluses of 0.5, 1 and 2.micrograms.kg-1 hexarelin as well as placebo.
The mean peak plasma growth hormone concentrations (Cmax) were 3.9, 26.9, 52.3, 55.0 ng.ml-1 after 0, 0.5, 1 and 2 micrograms.kg-1, respectively.

reviewFlags: acute GH pharmacodynamic endpoint only; no downstream clinical outcome (body composition, strength, disease outcome) was measured in this trial
small single-dose acute study (n=12); not generalizable to chronic subcutaneous self-administration protocols marketed online

claims.statement: In a rat model of myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury (left coronary artery ligation), subcutaneous hexarelin (100 mcg/kg/day for 7 days) improved cardiac systolic function, reduced malondialdehyde production, and increased surviving cardiomyocytes versus control, an effect blocked by a GHSR antagonist and attributed to interleukin-1 pathway modulation. This is preclinical rodent data and does not establish a cardioprotective effect in humans.

context.population: male Sprague-Dawley rats (animal model, not human)
context.doseText: 100 mcg/kg/day subcutaneously, twice daily dosing, for 7 days in a rat ischemia/reperfusion model (animal protocol; not a human dose recommendation)

extractedEvidence.quote: hexarelin treatment improved cardiac systolic function, decreased malondialdehyde production, and increased the number of surviving cardiomyocytes
down-regulation of IL-1β expression and up-regulation of IL-1Ra expression in I/R myocardium

reviewFlags: animal-only evidence (rat model); must not be presented as demonstrated human cardioprotective benefit
vendor and consumer content online extrapolates this rodent mechanism into human cardiac benefit claims without human trial support

claims.statement: Hexarelin has no FDA-approved drug product and, unlike some other GH secretagogue peptides (e.g. ipamorelin, GHRP-6), does not currently appear on FDA's published Category 2 list of bulk drug substances that may present significant safety risks for compounding; its regulatory status for 503A/503B compounding has not been affirmatively confirmed and should be re-checked against the live FDA list at review time.

context.population: prospective users of compounded or research-labeled hexarelin products

extractedEvidence.quote: Not FDA-approved. Banned in sport; research-only products are not approved for human use.

reviewFlags: absence from the FDA Category 2 table was confirmed by direct page fetch on 2026-08-28 but this list is revised periodically and must be re-verified at review time
no direct FDA compounding-substance evaluation document (e.g. PCAC briefing) for hexarelin was located in this pass

claims.statement: Hexarelin (listed as examorelin) is named explicitly under WADA's S2.2.4 Growth Hormone Releasing Factors category of the Prohibited List, alongside other GHRPs (GHRP-1/2/3/4/5/6) and GH secretagogues, and is therefore prohibited at all times in professional and Olympic-level sport.

context.population: athletes subject to WADA-code anti-doping rules

claims.statement: Hexarelin is marketed online by peptide vendors with a broad list of purported human benefits -- faster recovery and hypertrophy, increased lipolysis, joint/tendon healing, improved sleep, cardioprotection, and bone/skin effects from 'multi-cycle use' -- none of which are supported by controlled human trial evidence located in this review; the only controlled human data available addresses acute growth-hormone pharmacodynamics, and the cardioprotection claim specifically originates from a rat ischemia/reperfusion study, not human outcomes data.

context.useCase: muscle recovery, fat loss, joint healing, sleep, cardioprotection, anti-aging marketing claims

extractedEvidence.quote: Faster recovery between sessions, higher work capacity, modest hypertrophy when combined with training and protein intake
CD36 activation produces cardioprotective effects in ischemia-reperfusion and heart failure studies; unique to hexarelin within the GHRP class

reviewFlags: misinformation-adjacent: vendor page extrapolates a rat cardioprotection study directly into a human benefit claim without qualifying the species
no controlled human trial for hypertrophy, fat loss, joint healing, sleep, or cardioprotection endpoints was located for hexarelin in this pass

dosing protocols quoted on vendor pages (e.g. 50-200 mcg multiple times daily, cyclical schedules) are self-administration marketing content, not clinical protocol, and must not be reproduced as guidance

claims.statement: Beyond growth hormone release, hexarelin has been reported in the endocrinology literature to also stimulate cortisol and prolactin release and to activate the hypothalamo-pituitary-adrenal axis, indicating effects beyond the GH axis alone that carry safety and monitoring relevance for any human use.

context.population: human study subjects in endocrine pharmacology research

extractedEvidence.quote: Possible concerns include GH-axis side effects, glucose changes, water retention, and pituitary-hormone effects.

reviewFlags: this safety summary is drawn from a consumer-health secondary source, not a primary trial or label; a primary-literature source for cortisol/prolactin/HPA-axis effects (e.g. a PubMed-indexed human study) should be added on independent review
safety-critical claim requiring field authority sign-off before publication

conflicts.summary: Vendor marketing content presents hexarelin's CD36-mediated cardioprotection as an established effect ('cardioprotective effects in ischemia-reperfusion and heart failure studies'), while the only located supporting study is a rat ischemia/reperfusion model; no human cardioprotection trial was found in this pass.

reviewReasons: Expansion-batch evidence packet requires human review before publication.
No FDA PCAC briefing document or bulk-substance evaluation specific to hexarelin was located in this pass; confirm whether one exists before finalizing regulatory claims.
UNII, RxNorm, DrugBank, and ChEMBL identifiers not yet resolved from structured databases.

Human evidence is thin: only one controlled human study was located (acute IV GH-release pharmacodynamics, n=12); no human data on chronic subcutaneous use, cardioprotection, body composition, or safety in the populations that self-administer it.
WADA prohibited-status claim was sourced via a secondary mirror (Drugs.com) rather than the primary wada-ama.org document; verify against the current official list.
